page.title: Other systems
page.description: Send events between hosts in one process or many: a transport you write carries each send as a message, and the other host takes it.

hero.headline: Connect hosts over any wire.
hero.lede: An actor sends to an actor of another host by its address. Your transport carries the message, over a socket, a queue, HTTP or postMessage.

section.heading: A send to another system reaches your transport.
section.p: A host is one system, named by its system option. An actor can send to an actor of another system, in this process or on another machine, by its address.
The address is tinyactors://<system>/..., and the host decides whether an address is its own.
A send to another system goes to your transport, a handler that carries it there. The other side gives it to its host with host.send.
The transport and the wire are yours. An application of one host needs none of this page (Wire format).

section.heading: A message carries a send between hosts.
section.p: Each send to another system reaches the transport handler as a Send, whose target and origin are Addresses.
Its message is the outgoing half: target, event, data, sendid, origin and traceparent, null for a field the send lacks.
The receiving side passes it to host.send(message) as it is, in this process or in another binding's. A Python host takes it too.
On a wire, encode writes the message with its addresses as CBOR's tag 32, as a Python host's encode does. decode reads them back as Addresses.

example.code: charging 12 for tinyactors://shop/#_scxml_1 approved by tinyactors://bank/#_scxml_1

section.p: The teller answers to _event.origin, the sender's full address, so the answer goes back through the bank's transport.

section.heading: The transport reports what it cannot deliver.
section.p: While the handler runs, send.fail() reports a send that cannot be delivered. Later, on the sending host, host.fail(sender, sendid) does.
There sender is the message's origin, the actor that sent it, not its target. The sender gets error.communication with that sendid.
Delivery that worked needs no answer. Without a transport handler, each send to another system is failed.

section.heading: An input's target may be an address.
section.p: An actor's address is actor.address, and host.actor(address) finds the actor of a local one.
host.send takes an Actor, a session, an address string or an Address. The host resolves a local address, tinyactors://shop/@teller on the host named shop, to its actor.
A message's origin is the sender's address as the other side gave it, and becomes the event's _event.origin.

section.heading: Turn off Nagle's algorithm on sockets.
section.p: Across processes, a transport writes each message as a frame on a connection. Here a frame is four bytes of length and the message's CBOR.
Over TCP, call socket.setNoDelay(true) on both ends. The frames are small, and an answer is often a frame too.

With Nagle's algorithm on, Node.js's default, a second small write waits for the peer's delayed acknowledgement before it leaves. That wait is about 40 ms on Linux's loopback, and Python's asyncio turns the algorithm off by itself.
The transport reports a frame it cannot write, or a peer that is gone. It calls send.fail() while its handler runs, host.fail(origin, sendid) after.

section.heading: Read an address into its parts.
section.p: new Address(text) reads an address into its system, session (a bigint) and name, each undefined when the text lacks it.
Address.fromSession(system, session) and Address.fromName(system, name) make one, and toString() gives its text.

example.code: tinyactors://shop/#_scxml_42 shop 42n tinyactors://shop/@front%20desk front desk undefined

section.heading: A message goes through JSON as it is.
section.p: JSON.stringify writes an address as its text (address.toJSON()), and new Address(text) reads it back. So the other side's host.send takes a send.message that went through JSON.
Inside event data an address is plain text: values have no address type.

section.heading: Encode and parse SCXML's BasicHTTP.
section.p: SCXML defines BasicHTTP, an HTTP processor whose events travel as form posts. The package has its codec, for an I/O processor or a server of your own.

item.text: Writes the request a send makes, as bytes for a socket.
Reads an incoming request's form fields and its event: the _scxmleventname field, or HTTP.<METHOD>.

example.code: POST /scxml HTTP/1.1 POST /scxml order.placed sku=tea qty=2

section.p: The host does no HTTP itself: your program sends the bytes and serves the port.
